title: What To Do If You Are Scammed Online
summary: The first 24 hours matter most. Here is how to report online fraud and try to get your money back.

body.text: Online fraud moves fast. Money is often routed through several accounts within minutes, so what you do in the first hour really matters.

items: Call the national cyber helpline 1930 immediately.
Report on the official portal cybercrime.gov.in.
Inform your bank and ask them to freeze the transaction or the account.
Change your passwords and switch on two-factor authentication.

body.text: Do not contact the scammer again, and never pay any 'release fee' or 'processing charge' to recover money. That is a second scam.
The 'golden hour' is the short window right after a fraud. Reporting within it gives the best chance of freezing the money before it moves on.

items: Screenshots of the chat, profile or payment page.
Transaction IDs, UPI reference numbers and bank SMS.
Phone numbers, email IDs, links and account numbers involved.

body.text: You can file an online complaint even if you are not sure it is a crime. Reporting helps you and protects others.

practicalSteps: Act within the first hour if possible.
Dial 1930 and file a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in.
Give your bank the transaction reference in writing and ask for a written acknowledgement.
If the money is not restored, escalate to the RBI Ombudsman for your bank.
exceptions: If the loss is small and the bank refuses to act, a consumer or civil route may be faster than a criminal case.
Some states run their own cyber cells in addition to the national portal.

faqs.q: Can I get my money back?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If the fraud is reported quickly and the money is still traceable in a bank account, it can be frozen and returned. The longer you wait, the harder it becomes.

faqs.q: Will my complaint be kept private?
faqs.a: Yes. The official portal allows anonymous reporting for some categories, and your details are used to investigate the case.

sources.label: Ministry of Electronics and IT (IT Act, 2000)

misconceptions.myth: I can just ask the scammer to return my money.
misconceptions.fact: Scammers rarely return money and often ask for more. Stop contact and report to 1930.
